newsitem.title: USA: Lincoln National sees 1998 EPS dilution.
newsitem.headline: Lincoln National sees 1998 EPS dilution.

text.p: The sale of American States Financial Corp would dilute the earnings of parent Lincoln National Corp in 1998, but a planned stock buyback and possible acquisitions would mitigate that dilution, a top Lincoln National executive said.
American States, which is 83.3 percent owned by Lincoln National, earlier on Monday said it agreed to a $2.8 billion buyout offer from SAFECO Corp.

Lincoln National chief executive Ian Rolland, in a telephone interview with Reuters, said that the 1998 First Call analysts' estimate of $5.06 a share would be diluted by about 7.6 percent, assuming a $500 million stock buyback in 1997 and investment of proceeds from the deal at 4.5 percent after tax.
"Now to the extent we're able to do acquisitions that beat that 4.5 percent after tax target, that then mitigates the dilution and makes it even less than this," Rolland said.
"And I would say we really think it should not be difficult to do life and annuity acquisitions that beat that target," Rolland said.
Lincoln National is most interested in life insurance and annuity acquisitions that would help it expand the distribution of its products, Rolland said.
In the life insurance sector, Rolland said, the company would consider possible targets in both the United States and the United Kingdom.
Rolland declined to say whether the company was in talks with any prospective targets and said the company has not specified any timeframe in which it hopes to accomplish the acquisitions.
In addition to life insurance and annuity deals, Lincoln National also would consider making investment management acquisitions, specifically in the mutual fund sector.
Since 1990, Lincoln National has made a series of divestitures and acquisitions as part of its transformation into a more focused financial services company.
Rolland said Lincoln National is now comfortable with its current lineup of businesses and said he believes they all fit in with the company's overall strategy.
